title: Queering the Audits: Community-Based Auditing of AI Harms to Queer Communities
abstract: arXiv:2611.00345v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI systems embed majority-group defaults into training data, evaluation metrics, and category definitions, producing documented harms for queer communities including erasure, misclassification, and discrimination. Standard technical audits often rely on aggregate measures and cannot detect harms that be come visible only through the lived experience of affected communities. We conducted a participatory auditing workshop at EurIPS 2025 where 16 queer community members audited four case studies using the 4Cs harm taxonomy (Content, Conduct, Contact, Contract) applied across the AI lifecycle. Participants used structured worksheets and plenary synthesis to classify harms and trace them to their origins in the development pipeline. Across all four cases, participants traced harms to problem definition and data collection, and they identified contractual structures that extract value from vulnerable populations while providing minimal recours

translated_title: 酷儿化审计：针对酷儿群体AI伤害的社区参与式审计
translated_abstract: AI系统将多数群体的默认设置嵌入到训练数据、评估指标和类别定义之中，对酷儿群体造成了有据可查的伤害，包括抹除、错误分类和歧视。标准的技术审计通常依赖聚合性指标，无法检测到只有通过受影响社区的生活体验才能显现的伤害。我们在EurIPS 2025举办了一场参与式审计工作坊，16名酷儿社区成员运用贯穿AI全生命周期的4C伤害分类法（内容Content、行为Conduct、接触Contact、合同Contract）对四个案例研究进行了审计。参与者借助结构化工作表和全体综合讨论，对伤害进行分类并将其追溯至开发流程中的源头。在所有四个案例中，参与者都将伤害追溯到问题定义和数据收集阶段，并识别出从弱势群体中攫取价值却几乎不提供补救途径的合同结构。
tldr: 该研究通过让16名酷儿社区成员在参与式工作坊中运用4C伤害分类法审计四个AI案例，揭示了技术审计无法发现的社区伤害，并将伤害根源追溯到问题定义、数据收集及从弱势群体攫取价值的合同结构。
en_tdlr: This study engaged 16 queer community members in a participatory auditing workshop using the 4Cs harm taxonomy to audit four AI case studies, uncovering harms invisible to technical audits and tracing their roots to problem definition, data collection, and contractual structures that extract value from vulnerable populations.
